title: BurstProof SLO control snapshot
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, shareable snapshot comparing three SLO-control configurations under microburst vs steady-state traffic. The goal is not final numbers but to surface behavioral differences that affect product rollout and cost tradeoffs.

Short summary (tl;dr):
- Aggressive-prefetch keeps median latency low during 50–200 qps bursts but increases per-token GPU utilization by ~18% (higher cost).
- Session-stickiness (pinning to warm session containers) reduces cold-penalty 95/99 but increases tail under contention when many sessions overlap.
- Opportunistic-relaxed-SLO reduces expected cost by letting p99 drift, helpful for best-effort tiers; not suitable for revenue-facing interactive features.

Setup and assumptions:
- Model: Llama-3-13B v1 (fp16, int8 quantized path for some runs).
- Hardware: mixed cluster: A100-40GB (hot), A10G (warm), T4 (fallback).
- Workloads:
  * Microburst: baseline idle, then spike to 180 qps for 30s every 5 minutes, arrival jitter 0–30ms.
  * Sustained: steady 80 qps for 10 minutes.
  * Sessionized chat: average session length 6 turns, turn token count 120.
- Metrics collected: p50/p95/p99 latency (server-side), GPU utilization, tokens/sec served, cost estimate (GPU-minutes * spot price proxy), KV cache hit rate.
- Batching: continuous batching enabled with max batch size 32; for session-stickiness we clamp batch size to session affinity to avoid cross-session cache churn.
- Warmup: warm pool min 2 replicas per tenant for aggressive-prefetch; dynamic for others.

Configurations tested:
1) aggressive-prefetch (AP): pre-allocates warm containers, prefetches common KV prefixes, proactive kernel priming.
2) session-stickiness (SS): session affinity for request routing, longer container lifetime for pinned sessions.
3) opportunistic-relaxed-slo (ORS): allows internal scheduling to deprioritize best-effort requests during bursts, target p95 only for best-effort.

Representative results (median of 5 runs each, numbers are illustrative for quick triage):

Microburst (180 qps, 30s spikes):
- AP: p50=72ms, p95=210ms, p99=510ms, GPU util=72%, tokens/sec=12.4k, cost-index=1.18, kv-hitrate=0.62
- SS: p50=95ms, p95=260ms, p99=840ms, GPU util=59%, tokens/sec=11.2k, cost-index=1.00, kv-hitrate=0.71
- ORS: p50=140ms, p95=520ms, p99=1200ms, GPU util=48%, tokens/sec=9.6k, cost-index=0.78, kv-hitrate=0.45

Sustained (80 qps):
- AP: p50=65ms, p95=190ms, p99=420ms, GPU util=51%, tokens/sec=6.1k, cost-index=1.05, kv-hitrate=0.64
- SS: p50=70ms, p95=205ms, p99=470ms, GPU util=47%, tokens/sec=5.9k, cost-index=0.98, kv-hitrate=0.72
- ORS: p50=110ms, p95=300ms, p99=900ms, GPU util=39%, tokens/sec=5.1k, cost-index=0.75, kv-hitrate=0.40

Simple ASCII visualization (p95 during microburst):
- AP : ===================== (210ms)
- SS : ============================= (260ms)
- ORS: =============================================== (520ms)

Interpretation notes (quick):
- Aggressive-prefetch trades increased GPU utilization (and cost) for tighter p95 bounds during short spikes. The kernel priming reduces the initial token latency, and prewarming reduces cold starts.
- Session-stickiness is strong when users have consistent repeated turns (high kvcache reuse). It benefits p99 in sustained multi-turn flows but is vulnerable to resource fragmentation when many unique sessions spike simultaneously.
- Opportunistic-relaxed-SLO is the cheapest but shifts risk to tail percentiles. It's appropriate for background/async workloads or low-priority tiers.

What surprised us:
- KV cache hit rate drops significantly in ORS, which explains the double-digit hit on p95. This indicates that relaxed scheduling also reduces effective cache locality, not just queue priority.
- For microbursts, AP's cost penalty (~18% higher) is lower than expected given token-level uplift; the reason is throughput gains from fewer stalls.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Run the same configurations with Llama-3-70B quantized path to check scaling of cost penalties (expected bigger delta).
- Profile memory bandwidth during AP runs to see whether A100 hot lanes are the real cost driver (ticket INF-4212).
- Explore hybrid: AP for first N seconds of a burst then revert to ORS; simulate a phased policy.
- Confirm results in Dedicated (reserved capacity) vs Hosted (multi-tenant) to quantify isolation effects.

Actionable recommendations (short-term):
- For interactive paying-tier features, default to AP for the first 60 seconds after idle, then relax to SS or ORS based on observed session length.
- Add a telemetry flag to track runtime cache churn (per-session kv eviction rate) — useful to auto-select SS vs AP.
- Pilot ORS as an opt-in low-cost tier for long-running async summarization jobs.

Appendix: quick methodology checklist (for reproducibility)
- Seed traffic generator with same RNG seed for arrival jitter.
- Collect GPU metrics via telemetry-agent v2.7.1, trace spans exported to x-trace.
- Use cost-index = (GPU-minutes * region-spot-proxy) normalized to steady AP baseline.
- Record full latency histograms and raw traces to s3://perf-dumps/burstproof/sep21/ for later analysis.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working note, numbers are preliminary. Please comment inline with questions and anything we should run next.
- If anything here seems inconsistent with recent perf harness changes (PR linked above), flag and I'll gate re-runs.

-- Marcus

(End of snapshot)
